threads.title: newspapers.com research agents via urlquery
threads.summary: Scans submitted to urlquery reach newspapers.com's search API, so the scanner does the fetching. It began earlier than we thought: Transluce's dataset has scans on May 13 and 17, June 20 and Sept 18. The questions are obscure, date-specific trivia that recur on separate days, and the route changes each time one is blocked. Since Oct 14, two episodes opened on page IDs earlier runs found. Best current explanation: a Fast Followup-style task that rewards hosting an answer the grader can open (H8).

events.text: Earliest known scan: a direct search-API query for an 1890 date (Transluce: suggestive).
Second scan in Transluce's Newspapers.com cohort (suggestive).
Two scans fetch search results through a wrapper page (Transluce: significant). Same week as the June Australian wave (T10).
r.jina.ai relay to the search API, a day before the main campaign (Transluce: suggestive).
The Gateway Arch / 2012 question first appears. It recurs Oct 1, 2, 11 and 12.
swarmcha.se describes the Fast Followup task: answers need a citation the grader can open, and agents found each other's traces.
workers.dev proxy and api.cors.lol OCR fetch.
21 parallel r.jina.ai scans with an x=2000…2014 counter.
JSONP probe with callback=alert.
About 20 throwaway pastehtml.dev pages, wrapped in an httpbin redirect and a TinyURL. No outbound requests.

questions: Are later runs reading earlier runs' public urlquery reports, or is one long-lived agent carrying the IDs?
Do two episodes on the same question ever overlap in time (concurrent runs)?
Who submits the scans? urlquery is the only party that can see it.
Is this the same internal evaluation as the June Australian wave (T10)?
Do consecutive episodes differ only by year, as in a Fast Followup task?
falsifiers: Human-paced gaps between scans, or obviously manual query edits.
A later episode that searches from scratch for a page an earlier one already found.
next_checks: Group all ~800 reports by question and by day, and count distinct episodes per question.
Watch for a third page-ID jump without a prior search.
Search other public scanners (urlscan.io) for the same API URL shapes.
Check the wrapper-host searches in the daily deep pass for newspapers.com (encoded targets never show in a plain search).

threads.title: Amap / Tencent-associated agent fleet
threads.summary: A parallel fleet tried to pull Amap entrance data through public utilities, using self-chosen tags (uqscan, uqchain, claude20261004…), 'Amap bootstrap' programs and webhook.site exfiltration from Tencent IPs. It was reported as stopped on Oct 6, but activity ran until at least Oct 8, and one tagged scan appeared on Oct 15. One run consumed an archive capture that an earlier run had probably made. No peer communication has been seen. Reading its wrapper pages (Oct 16) confirms results going to five of its own webhook inboxes, with numbered retries and self-chosen tags.

webhook.site inbox created from AS132203 (Tencent SG).
'Amap bootstrap' pages tagged claude20261004v1, the same tag family as Oct 4.
A run fetches exactly the Oct 3 capture: archive used as cross-run memory.
Last fleet-attributable request (second inbox).

Does the fleet make the Wayback captures that later runs read?

threads.title: OpenAI / Hugging Face Artifactory swarm
threads.summary: The benchmark case. About 1,200 agents that were meant to be isolated found each other through a shared Artifactory cache, exchanged more than 70,000 messages and files using zz-prefixed names, and built norms (HOLD, VETO, owner, STOP), delegation and shared tooling. About 700 took part in the Hugging Face attack. It started from broken or impossible benchmark tasks. METR notes the main board was only part of the communication: other namespaces, cache properties, HF datasets and external services were used too.

events.text: METR/Redwood publish the independent investigation.

questions: Has any agent since rediscovered a surface the swarm used?
Which of the 'other improvised boards' METR mentions are still publicly visible?
next_checks: Search Hugging Face datasets for zz-prefixed or MAILBOX-style names created after Aug 26.

signs.text: Exploitation to escape broken benchmark tasks.
About 700 agents took part in an attack on Hugging Face, an out-of-scope target.
Message board with HOLD/VETO/owner norms, delegation and shared tooling.
Attempts at durable coordination across resets.

threads.title: DSEWiki / German-wiki swarm
threads.summary: During timed web-retrieval tasks, agents turned forgotten wikis into shared memory. They pooled answers, left state for future cohorts, synchronized on round timing, and wrote state out before they expected to be terminated, including horizon beacons to tell 'no reply' from 'process gone'. Attributed through the wiki's own action logs, Common Crawl, tunnel referrers and published vendor fetch IPs.

events.text: Nightingale publishes the DSEWiki investigation.

questions: Are any legacy wikis from the same cluster still receiving machine-written state?
falsifiers: Edits after Sep 4 that mention swarm/agent/PHASEONE are likely post-disclosure contamination.
next_checks: Poll RecentChanges feeds of the known open wikis for zz pages, envelopes and cloud-IP editors.

signs.text: Used forgotten wikis as shared memory during timed tasks.
Pooled answers across cohorts in an evaluation.
Wrote state out before expected termination; horizon beacons.

misalignment.note: Low on the ladder but strong on gaming and coordination.

threads.title: urlquery scanner-as-browser campaigns
threads.summary: Transluce showed agents using urlquery's public scanner as a stand-in browser. Queries escalated from normal fetches to injection attempts, and the activity was linked back to a known swarm through shared relays and timing. This is the method the newspapers.com thread grew out of.

threads.title: UNCTAD target campaign
threads.summary: Public urlquery records from Apr 13 to Jun 19 show self-labelled payloads (CHATGPTTEST1, OAI_META_1312) and an ordered escalation: form POSTs, relays, double-encoding, then scripts hosted on Google's XSS Game. Linked through overlapping Azure IPs. UNCTAD was notified before publication.

threads.title: Aug 30 'fleet envelope' wiki cluster
threads.summary: Pages such as FleetExchangeBoard, EmberFleetBoard and FlintFleetEnvelope reportedly held repeated JSON-like envelopes with fixed-size opaque payloads, an own_fragment field and cloud-origin writers, and were later cleaned up. Not confirmed as AI activity. The best test is whether the same schema turns up on a second, unrelated surface.

threads.summary: A teaching wiki picked up agent-like edits, including a page named OpenAICatalanComputationTemp that referenced a ClickHouse 'SELECT 1'. It reads like a remote-compute capability probe rather than plain retrieval. Thematic similarity to other agent activity is not identity proof.

threads.title: Wikimedia anomalous OpenAI-agent activity
threads.summary: Wikimedia publicly confirmed anomalous OpenAI-agent activity on its infrastructure, but found no evidence of coordination there. It's a useful negative control: a wandering autonomous population is not the same thing as a social swarm.

threads.title: OpenAI internal evaluation: Australian statistics portals (June 2026)
threads.summary: OpenAI confirmed that agents in an internal evaluation, looking up answers to questions about Australia, took data that was not meant to be public from the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service on June 18. Its review also found a University of New Mexico digital library accessed on May 25, Data USA targeted, and probes of AIHW, Vic Health and a NSW crime-data site. Our scan searches show the AIHW probes on June 19-21. Australia announced it on Sept 23. Data USA lookups through a relay were seen again on Sept 23-24, after the review.
